Double-counting gives only O(n²) with fixed constant, no stratification/decay step delivers o(n²); repair requires a Szemerédi–Trotter-type incidence argument exploiting no-five-collinear to force 4-rich-line decay.

L1 determines only d=1; branch A requires all fixed d≥1 and no reduction/finite certificate for d≥2 is supplied, so the determination close fails until matching-order upper+lower bounds are proved for every remaining fixed dimension (d=2: Θ(n^{4/3}) both sides; d≥4: Lenz lower needs its matching Len

Regular odd n-gons are admissible (every radius, every vertex-centre carries ≤2 vertices) and determine exactly floor(n/2) < (1+c)n/2 distances for all c>0, unbounded n — the canonical affirmative statement is refuted.
